licence.title: Physician Assistant License
licence.renewalDeadline: Annually, no later than 30 days after the PA's birthday
licence.compactNote: G.S. 90-9.3(a1) and Article 18J (PA Licensure Compact) are effective April 1, 2026, but NCMB states the compact is not yet operational; the traditional licence remains the pathway.

ce.cyclePeriodNote: Two-year CME period begins on the PA's birthday following issuance of the licence; licence itself renews annually
ce.categoryRules: All 50 hours must be NCCPA-recognized Category I CME

topicMandates.topic: Controlled substance prescribing practices, including chronic pain management
topicMandates.appliesTo: PAs who prescribe controlled substances; counts within the 50 hours; NOT waived by NCCPA certification unless part of the certification activity; MATE training satisfies it for the two-year period in which it was completed

ce.controlledSubstanceCe: 2 hours every 2-year CME period for controlled substance prescribers (21 NCAC 32S .0216(b))
ce.optionalTopicsThatQualify: Interprofessional, cultural competency and implicit bias courses count toward the 50 hours if NCCPA approved (optional, not a mandate)

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Signed supervisory arrangement statement kept at all practice sites (not filed; available to Board on request); Intent to Practice form filed with the Board; supervising physician meetings monthly for first 6 months of a new arrangement, then at least every 6 months, with signed written records. Team-based PAs (more than 4,000 hours as a PA plus more than 1,000 hours in the specialty, practicing in a team-based setting) apply to NCMB for team-based status and are not required to file an Intent to Practice.
practice.notes: Team-based practice (G.S. 90-9.3A, S.L. 2025-37 Part VI) took effect on the earlier of NCMB permanent rules or June 30, 2026, so it is in effect by 2026-10. Team-based PAs in perioperative settings remain physician supervised. Pain management practices are excluded from team-based settings.

prescribing.ceForPrescribers: 2 hours controlled substance prescribing CME per 2-year period (within the 50); DEA registration required to prescribe controlled substances; written prescribing instructions from the supervising physician at each site (non team-based)

board.name: North Carolina Board of Nursing (NP approval jointly with the North Carolina Medical Board)

rn.renewalDeadline: Last day of birth month, biennially
rn.ceNote: Continuing competence: attest to ONE learning option per cycle; options include national certification, 30 contact hours, or 15 contact hours plus a project/publication/presentation/640 practice hours. Each renewal also requires a self-assessment of practice and a learning plan; keep proof 3 years (21 NCAC 36 .0232(a),(d))

aprn.title: NP (Nurse Practitioner approval to practice)
aprn.separateLicenceOrCertificate: Approval to practice (registered with both boards), not a separate licence
aprn.renewalDeadline: Last day of the NP's birth month, annually
aprn.ceNote: At least 20 of the 50 hours must be within the NP's national certification and approved by a national credentialing body or ACCME; current national certification is deemed compliance; the 50 hour clock starts with the first renewal after initial approval; CE records kept 5 years

topicMandates.topic: Controlled substance prescribing (prescribing practices, chronic pain, abuse/misuse recognition, or non-opioid alternatives)
topicMandates.period: every 12 months (within the preceding 12 months before prescribing)
topicMandates.appliesTo: NPs who prescribe controlled substances; MATE training satisfies it for the two-year CE period completed

aprn.renewalNote: Renewal requires a current NC RN licence or a multistate privilege to practice, current national NP certification, CE attestation, fee and application (21 NCAC 36 .0806(a)).

prescribing.controlledSubstanceCe: 1 hour within the preceding 12 months before prescribing controlled substances (21 NCAC 36 .0807(b))
prescribing.notes: Own DEA number required; primary supervising physician must hold equal or greater DEA schedules; prescribable drugs listed in the collaborative practice agreement

practice.agreementType: collaborative practice agreement with a primary supervising physician
practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Signed by NP and primary supervising physician, kept at each practice site, reviewed at least yearly with a dated signature sheet; QI meetings at least every 6 months (monthly for the first 6 months); records retained 5 years. S.L. 2025-37 did not change NP supervision.

unverified: PA and NP state CS registration: G.S. 90-101(c)(6) exempts a 'practitioner' under G.S. 90-87(22)a, defined as a physician, dentist, optometrist, veterinarian, scientific investigator 'or other person licensed, registered or otherwise permitted' to dispense or administer controlled substances. PAs and NPs fit that general wording but are not named; value false is kept as a reading of the statute.
NP: ncbon.com still returns HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch (re-tested 2026-10), so Board of Nursing web pages were not cross-checked; all NP values rest on 21 NCAC 36 rule text loaded from OAH.
NP: 'restricted' is the AANP label; primary rules confirm physician supervision and a collaborative practice agreement (21 NCAC 36 .0802, .0810), not the label.
PA: NCMB has not codified team-based rules in 21 NCAC 32S as of the 2026-10 OAH index; the team-based application form and hour documentation standard are not yet confirmed.

PA and NP: no state topic mandate beyond controlled substance CE was found for opioid/pain, implicit bias, human trafficking, child abuse, ethics, HIV, end of life, Alzheimer, suicide prevention, infection control, cultural competency or domestic violence in 21 NCAC 32S, 21 NCAC 36 Section .0800 or the NCMB controlled substance CME page; a search result describing a 1-hour human trafficking course every six years referred to another state's law, not North Carolina.

Federal: the DEA one-time 8-hour MATE training applies to every DEA registrant nationally; in NC it also satisfies the state controlled substance CE for the CE period in which it is completed (PA .0216(c), NP .0807(c)).
corrections: PA: added 21 NCAC 32S .0216(d): cultural competency and implicit bias (and interprofessional) courses qualify toward the 50 hours when NCCPA approved; optional, not a mandate.

PA: recorded the .0216(c) exception as its own fact: an NCCPA-certified PA meets the 2-hour controlled substance CME inside certification activity only if that CME was part of the certification activity.

PA: added that team-based status requires an application to NCMB (NCMB page), that perioperative team-based PAs remain physician supervised (G.S. 90-9.3A(c)), and that pain management practices are excluded (G.S. 90-1.1(4d)c), each with its own primary quote.
PA: added PA Licensure Compact note: G.S. 90-9.3(a1)/Article 18J effective April 1, 2026, NCMB says the compact is not yet operational.

PA: the OAH 21 NCAC 32S rule index (loaded 2026-10) lists no team-based practice rule, so NCMB has not yet codified team-based rules; the statute is in force through the S.L. 2025-37 s.6.3 June 30, 2026 backstop (moved from unverified to confirmed).
NP: added that the RN prerequisite for NP renewal may be met by a multistate (compact) privilege, not only an NC RN licence (21 NCAC 36 .0806(a)(1)).
NP: added that the 50-hour CE period starts at the first renewal after initial approval and that CE records are kept 5 years (21 NCAC 36 .0807(a),(d)).
NP/RN: added the continuing competence self-assessment and learning plan required at every RN renewal and the 3-year proof retention (21 NCAC 36 .0232(a),(d)).
NP: confirmed against S.L. 2025-37 Part VI text that the 2025 reforms do not change NP supervision or collaborative practice agreements (only PA team-based practice and incidental NP references).
